newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SEC says insider trading charges settled.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SEC says insider trading charges settled.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday a Hong Kong man had settled agency charges of insider trading involving Renaissance Hotel Group N.V. shares and had agreed to pay a $2 million penalty.
Without admitting or denying wrong-doing, Frederick Liu, 35, also agreed to an order barring him from repeating the alleged offenses, the SEC said.
"We are very pleased that this has been resolved," said Donald Sunshine, a New York attorney representing Liu.
In a complaint filed in federal court in New York, the SEC alleged that Liu purchased 1.4 million Renaissance common shares on December 30 and 31, 1996.
Later on December 31, it was announced that Doubletree Corp had reached an agreement to acquire Renaissance.

The SEC alleged Liu purchased the shares at an average cost of $15.66 each. "As a result of the announcement of the proposed deal, the value of the 1.4 million shares increased by $11,270,000," it said.

The SEC further alleged that on January 2, after learning that the SEC had authorized an emergency lawsuit charging him with illegal insider trading, Liu cancelled the stock trades and abandoned the trading profits.

The SEC did not disclose how Liu learned of the pending acquisition announcement. However, Jerry Isenberg, the SEC attorney handling the case, said the size of Liu's transaction helped point the agency to the alleged wrong-doing.
"We were ready to sue him and what we did led to his cancellation of the trade," Isenberg said.
The SEC is seeking just the $2 million penalty because Liu never collected on the profits, Isenberg said.
The merger between Renaissance and Doubletree was never finalized.
Renaissance has since been acquired by Marriott International Inc.
